div.head: IV As 6
div.ab: [De fure capto, qui personam vel locum pacis adierit.] [Q/Br] Et sit fur qui furatus est postquam concilium fuit apud Ðunresfeld vel furetur, nullo modo vita dignus habeatur; non per socnam, non per pecuniam, si per verum reveletur in eo; sit liber, sit servus, sic comitum, sic villanorum, sit domina, sit pedissequa, sit quicumque sit, sic handhabbenda, sic non handhabbenda; si pro certo sciatur—id est si verbum non dixerit ut andsaca sit—vel in ordalio reus sit, vel per aliud aliquid [culpabilis] innotescat.

And if there is a thief who has committed theft since the Council was held at Thundersfield, and is still engaged in thieving, he shall in no way be judged worthy of life, neither by claiming the right to protection, nor by making monetary payment, if the charge is truly substantiated against him—whether it is a freeman or a slave, a noble or commoner, or, if it is a woman, whether she is a mistress or a maid—whosoever it may be, whether taken in the act, or not taken in the act, if it is known for a certainty—that is, if he shall not make a statement of denial—or if the charge is proved in the ordeal, or if his guilt becomes known in any other way.
